workingHypotheses: Yoti is probably too broad for one linear case study; the strongest story may be a system of trust told through three concrete artefacts.

organisingIdea.statement: Make invisible digital proof feel trustworthy at the exact moment a person or verifier has to act on it.

claims.statement: Yoti aimed to make digital identity feel secure, private, intelligible, and usable across online and offline contexts.
claims.notes: This is company-level context; the case study still needs a bounded project.

claims.statement: The work addressed consumers proving identity or age, third-party businesses requesting data, in-store staff, and internal stakeholders.
claims.notes: Choose one primary audience per chapter or narrow the case study.

claims.statement: Alexander worked as a Senior Product Designer across product, engineering, brand, and design-system work.
claims.notes: Separate ownership by artefact and team.

claims.statement: The CV dates Alexander's Yoti employment from December 2017 to November 2019.
claims.notes: Conflicts with the old portfolio's 'over two and a half years' statement.

claims.statement: Portfolio v1 says the work spanned over two and a half years.
claims.notes: Resolve against employment dates and any freelance or prior involvement.

claims.statement: Alexander co-developed the design system and style guide and helped maintain cohesion across product, engineering, and brand.
claims.notes: Clarify co-founder language, governance, and lasting contribution.

claims.statement: Alexander says he designed and prototyped a gyroscope-driven, spoof-resistant hologram for in-store age proof.
claims.notes: Strong personal-contribution story; confirm collaborators and technical implementation.

claims.statement: The old portfolio claims the hologram progressed from R&D prototype to production and remained in use in May 2025.
claims.notes: Verify present status and publication permission.

claims.statement: Other attributed work includes a low-cost physical ID scanner, third-party QR login, an age-verification recovery effort, the main website, and content strategy.
claims.notes: This breadth should be separated into discrete artefacts during interview.

claims.statement: Policy change, public scepticism, privacy concerns, spoof resistance, and unfamiliar interaction models made trust the central design constraint.
claims.notes: Strong narrative frame if anchored to a specific journey.

claims.statement: The factsheet names Andy Ainger, Amy Rodgers, a partially redacted brand lead, and a partially redacted head of development as collaborators.
claims.notes: Incomplete names mean no public credit can be drafted yet.

claims.statement: The CV claims privacy-first onboarding reduced drop-off, while Portfolio v1 claims several systems remained in use.
claims.notes: Neither outcome has supporting metrics or current verification.

conflicts.question: Was Alexander's Yoti involvement approximately two years or more than two and a half years?
